items.summary: the three leaders posed together at APEC before talks that the White House says will cover the Iran war and a possible three-way nuclear arms agreement. Ukraine is not expected on the formal agenda, since Xi reportedly sees it as a European matter.
items.matters: the US-China trade truce runs to 10 January 2027 and New START lapsed in February, so analysts expect few concrete results beyond symbolism.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Russia's President Vladimir Putin, China's President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump pose for a group photo with other world leaders during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China [Sergei Bobylev/Pool Photo via AP] By Heba Habib Published On 19 Nov 2026 19 Nov 2026 US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin will hold a three-way meeting on Thursday in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, the first ever between the leaders of the world’s three most powerful militaries.

The meeting, which will take place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, has drawn comparisons with the 1945 wartime Yalta conference at which the United States, United Kingdom and then-Soviet Union agreed on the post-war order. But those powers had been allied during a world war. Analysts say the three men meeting on Thursday are arriving with very different goals, and that few concrete outcomes can be expected.

“It’s a summit of Trump’s ego, Putin’s tactics, China’s strategy,” Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera.

The trilateral meeting is taking place on the sidelines of the APEC leaders’ summit, which China is hosting in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19. Trump travelled to China after attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) meeting in Manila.

The White House has said that Trump plans to discuss the war with Iran as well as a possible three-way agreement on nuclear armament with Xi and Putin. Ukraine is not expected to be on the formal agenda, as Xi is understood to be reluctant to be drawn into what he views as a European matter.

The meeting comes as Trump has strained ties with traditional US allies, at times floating troop withdrawals from South Korea and cuts to assistance for Japan, while his administration continues to describe China as Washington’s main geopolitical rival.

Vuk Vuksanovic, a lecturer in foreign policy and grand strategy at the Department of War Studies, King’s College, London, cautioned against viewing the summit as a new “carve-up” of the world order, however.

At the Yalta Conference in February 1945, US President Franklin D Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Crimea to shape the post-war order, agreeing on the division of Germany and setting the stage for Soviet influence over Eastern Europe.

items.headline: The ICJ rules today on the Rohingya genocide case against Myanmar
items.summary: The Gambia accuses Myanmar of genocide over the 2017 crackdown that displaced at least 730,000 Rohingya. The court must decide whether the state acted with intent to destroy the group.
items.matters: it is the court's first genocide merits judgment in over a decade, and legal experts say its reasoning could affect South Africa's case against Israel.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Rohingya refugee children fly improvised kites at the Kutupalong refugee camp near Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh [File: Damir Sagolj/Reuters] By Rached El-Moctar Published On 19 Nov 2026 19 Nov 2026 The top court of the United Nations is scheduled to rule on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority in a case brought by the West African nation of The Gambia.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague is to deliver its verdict on Thursday in what will be its first judgement on the merits of a genocide case in more than a decade.

Legal experts said the ruling could bear on South Africa’s ongoing case accusing Israel of genocide in Gaza, which Israel is contesting.

The Gambia accuses Myanmar of seeking to destroy the Rohingya people during a 2017 military crackdown that forced hundreds of thousands to flee. Myanmar, meanwhile, claims it was responding to attacks by fighters from the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) on police posts.

Myanmar’s military began what it called clearance operations in Rakhine State in October 2016 and a far larger campaign in August 2017 after attacks on police posts by a Rohingya armed group. About 10,000 Rohingya were killed and 740,000 forced to flee to Bangladesh, the UN estimated.

UN investigators found that soldiers razed hundreds of villages, carried out mass killings and routinely raped and gang-raped Rohingya women, girls and boys. They said the sexual violence indicated genocidal intent.

The military itself has announced convictions in only two cases brought after the violence. However, in one, seven soldiers jailed for killing 10 Rohingya men and boys at Inn Din village were freed after serving less than a year of their 10-year sentences.

In 1982, long before the crackdown, Myanmar excluded the Rohingya from its 135 recognised ethnic groups, calling them immigrant Bengalis despite many families having lived in Myanmar for generations. Nearly all Rohingya have been denied citizenship since then, making them the world’s largest stateless group.

Since fighting with the military resumed in 2023, the Arakan Army, an ethnic Rakhine armed group, has taken most of the state. The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights said in August that both forces have committed widespread and systematic abuses against the Rohingya, accusing the Arakan Army of torture, sexual violence and forced recruitment.

items.headline: European leaders meet in Berlin as Kyiv faces a €25bn funding gap
items.summary: Merz hosts the Coalition of the Willing with Macron, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and more than 30 leaders, with Zelenskyy attending. The Commission has proposed a further €45bn loan for 2027, up to €25bn for military aid and €20bn for budget support, and even with it a €25bn gap remains.
items.matters: Poland adds no new PURL money for now, and Bulgaria, Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia are opting out of the next round of EU financing.

x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, right, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy shake hands during a news conference at the Chancellery in Berlin on November 3, 2026 [Ralf Hirschberger/AFP] By Kristen Talman Published On 19 Nov 2026 19 Nov 2026 As US President Donald Trump shakes hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China, European leaders are due to gather in Berlin to agree on funding for Ukraine’s defence and press Washington’s visiting envoys for a European role in Russia-Ukraine peace talks.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is hosting the so-called Coalition of the Willing summit on Thursday alongside French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. More than 30 leaders are expected to attend, including Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

The summit agenda includes long-term security guarantees and continued military and financial support for Ukraine. Zelenskyy has said air defence will be his immediate priority as Kyiv enters a winter with the threat of Moscow’s drone attacks looming.

Trump administration envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected, according to media reports, to meet Ukrainian officials and Europe’s newly formed negotiating team in Berlin. The team includes France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy and Poland, plus European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa.

Washington has backed European participation in the next round of talks, but Moscow has yet to agree.

The impasse could put Ukraine’s main financial backer on the sidelines of talks over its future, as European Union countries are set to make even steeper commitments.

The European Commission on Wednesday proposed an additional 45 billion-euro ($49.3bn) loan for 2027, with up to 25 billion euros ($27.4bn) for military aid and 20 billion euros ($21.9bn) for budget support. That follows a 1.71 billion-euro ($1.87bn) payment on Monday under an existing EU loan for drones, ammunition and air defence.

Even if the new loan is approved, it would leave a 25 billion-euro ($27.4bn) financing gap next year.

Zelenskyy said the US envoys had promised to brief Kyiv on Trump’s discussions in China, where he is meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and Putin.

The Berlin summit gives European negotiators a chance to agree on what they want from the next round and put it directly to Trump’s envoys, just days after a public disagreement between the transatlantic partners emerged in Brussels.

items.headline: W Kancelarii Prezydenta powstał jeden wspólny projekt w sprawie TK
items.summary: Zbigniew Bogucki mówi, że bazą jest najdalej idący projekt PSL, mocno uzupełniony pomysłami innych klubów, a uczestnicy zgadzają się co do około 70% rozwiązań. Trzecie spotkanie jest dziś o 18:00, a KO i Lewica na nie nie odpowiedziały.
items.matters: bez KO i Lewicy projekt nie ma szans na większość, a zmiana konstytucji wymaga dwóch trzecich głosów w Sejmie.
items.body:
Skomentuj W Kancelarii Prezydenta powstał jeden projekt ws. Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, łączący pomysły w tej sprawie zgłoszone przez środowiska polityczne - przekazał w środę szef KPRP Zbigniew Bogucki po spotkaniu z politykami ws. TK. Dodał, że kolejne takie spotkanie odbędzie się w czwartek o godz. 18.

fot. Jacek Szydlowski / Forum / / FORUM W środę po spotkaniu w KPRP z przedstawicielami m.in. PiS, Rozwoju Plus, PSL, Konfederacji, Polski 2050, Razem, Konfederacji Korony Polskiej czy Demokracji Bezpośredniej Bogucki poinformował, że zgodnie z zapowiedziami powstał jeden wspólny projekt ws. rozwiązania sytuacji wokół TK.

W kontekście jednego wspólnego projektu Bogucki powiedział, że „najdalej idący” projekt PSL ws. TK został „mocno uzupełniony” o propozycje innych klubów i kół parlamentarnych.

Zapowiedział, że kolejna rozmowa ugrupowań i KPRP ws. TK odbędzie się w czwartek o godz. 18 w Kancelarii Prezydenta. Będzie to już trzecie spotkanie klubów i kół z Boguckim ws. Trybunału.

Relacjonując przebieg środowego spotkania, Bogucki powiedział, że wraz z obecnymi przedstawicielami ugrupowań są zgodni „w około 70 proc.” co do rozwiązań dotyczącym TK oraz „incydentalnych zmian, które pozwoliłyby zażegnać głęboki kryzys wokół Trybunału”.

Dodał, że na środowym spotkaniu pojawiły się wszystkie kluby i koła, które brały udział w poniedziałkowych rozmowach. Podkreślił, że wszyscy zadeklarowali też obecność na spotkaniu w czwartek. Dodał, że KO, Lewica i Centrum nie odpowiedziały na zaproszenie na środowe spotkanie.

Jak mówił, celem prac ws. TK jest stworzenie projektu, który będzie „do zaakceptowania przez tę większość bezwzględną, która się gromadzi” podczas spotkań ugrupowań z KPRP.

Dopytywany o dalsze konsultacje w sprawie TK, odparł, że spotkania planowane są z dnia na dzień. Dodał przy tym, że dynamika rozmów jest bardzo duża. - Będziemy robić wszystko, żeby te rozmowy trwały i zmierzały do finału, czyli pakietu rozwiązań, które zaakceptują wszystkie środowiska - zapewniał Bogucki.

Bogucki poinformował też, że będzie obecny na organizowanych w czwartek w Sejmie przez PSL konsultacjach społecznych w sprawie projektu zmian Konstytucji RP.

Pytany o decyzję sędziów TK ws. pozbawienia immunitetu Bogdana Święczkowskiego i Bartłomieja Sochańskiego, Bogucki odparł, że to „fatalna decyzja”. - Ona jest bez podstaw prawnych, jest w kontrze do prawa, konstytucji, logiki prawnej, a także w kontrze do elementarnej logiki - ocenił.

items.headline: Prezydent zawetował podwyżkę VAT do 23% na napoje energetyzujące z sokiem i bezalkoholowe piwo oraz wino
items.summary: Nawrocki pytał, jak to się mieści w logice rządu, który podnosi akcyzę na alkohol, i powołał się na sadowników, bo te napoje zużywają około 30 tys. ton polskich jabłek.
items.matters: według oceny skutków regulacji budżet traci przez to około 1,3 mld zł w 2027 r. i około 15,8 mld zł w latach 2027–2036.
items.body:
Skomentuj W środę prezydent Karol Nawrocki poinformował, że zawetował nowelizację ustawy o podatku od towarów i usług, której celem było podniesienie stawki VAT do 23 proc. na zawierające sok napoje energetyczne i bezalkoholowe odpowiedniki napojów alkoholowych.

fot. Daniel Dmitriew / / FORUM Prezydent w wystąpieniu wideo, które zostało zamieszczone na profilu Kancelarii Prezydenta RP na platformie X, jako powody weta wskazał skutki gospodarcze podwyżki i wątpliwości dotyczące celu podwyżki oraz brak gwarancji przeznaczenia wpływów na ochronę zdrowia.

„(...) bo z jednej strony proponuje się podwyżkę akcyzy na alkohol, a z drugiej podwyżkę VAT na produkty, które mogą zastępować napoje alkoholowe. Jak to mieści się w logice działania rządu?” – powiedział prezydent Nawrocki.

Dodał, że w sprawie ustawy otrzymał wiele opinii od organizacji reprezentujących rolników i sadowników. Zwrócił uwagę, że do produkcji napojów zawierających sok, które miałaby odjąć podwyżka VAT, wykorzystuje się 30 tys. ton polskich jabłek i tysiące ton innych owoców.

„Wyższy podatek mógłby obniżyć sprzedaż, skłonić producentów do zmiany receptur i zmniejszyć zapotrzebowanie na polskie owoce” – ocenił prezydent.

Zawetowana ustawa miała podnieść do 23 proc. stawkę VAT na napoje energetyzujące zawierające sok oraz bezalkoholowe piwa i wina zawierające sok. Chodzi o napoje, które zawierają w swoim składzie co najmniej 20 proc. soku owocowego, warzywnego lub owocowo-warzywnego. Weto prezydenta oznacza, że utrzymana zostanie stawka 5 proc. w obrocie handlowym i 8 proc. w gastronomii.

items.headline: Fed minutes turn hawkish
items.summary: nearly all participants said further rate rises may be appropriate and some would back a move larger than 25 bp, after the 10-2 vote that held rates at 3.75-4.00% with Cook and Hammack wanting a hike. Gold fell more than 3% to about $3,730 an ounce, its lowest since September 2025, and the 10-year yield dropped 4 bp to 5.05%.
items.matters: the next decision on 8–9 December comes with new projections, and many officials flagged AI-sector growth as an inflation risk.
items.body:

"Jeśli chodzi o perspektywy polityki pieniężnej w nadchodzących miesiącach, niemal wszyscy uczestnicy posiedzenia uznali, że przy założeniu realizacji bazowych prognoz dotyczących inflacji oraz rynku pracy, zasadne może być dalsze podnoszenie przedziału docelowego dla stopy funduszy federalnych, aby zapewnić terminowy powrót inflacji do celu wynoszącego 2 proc." - napisano w protokole z posiedzenia Rezerwy Federalnej USA 27-28 października.

"Niektórzy uczestnicy posiedzenia wskazali, że jeśli napływające dane o inflacji okażą się niekorzystne, podczas kolejnego posiedzenia warto rozważyć podwyżkę stóp o więcej niż 25 pb. Kilku uczestników posiedzenia zauważyło, że inflacja może okazać się bardziej trwała, niż przewidywano. W takiej sytuacji konieczne mogłoby stać się przyjęcie bardziej restrykcyjnego nastawienia w polityce pieniężnej. Uczestnicy posiedzenia podkreślili, że przyszłe decyzje będą uzależnione od napływających danych, zmieniających się prognoz oraz bilansu ryzyk" - dodano.

"Niektórzy uczestnicy posiedzenia zauważyli, że oczekiwania rynku co do zaostrzenia polityki w grudniu i w przyszłym roku były w dużej mierze zgodne z ich własnymi ocenami właściwej ścieżki dla stóp proc. Kilku z nich uznało tę zbieżność za czynnik ograniczający ryzyko związane z utrzymaniem obecnego bez zmian przedziału stóp proc. na tym posiedzeniu. Kilku uczestników posiedzenia, choć poparło utrzymanie dotychczasowego przedziału stopy funduszy federalnych, zaznaczyło, że decyzja ta była trudna do podjęcia" - wynika z minutes.

"Uczestnicy posiedzenia ocenili, że średnio- i długoterminowe oczekiwania inflacyjne pozostają spójne z celem Komitetu. Kilku z nich zwróciło jednak uwagę, że krótkoterminowe oczekiwania inflacyjne, mierzone na podstawie danych rynkowych oraz ankiet, wzrosły. Wskazali również, że wskaźniki rynkowe (oparte na wycenie papierów wartościowych indeksowanych wskaźnikiem CPI) mogą być obecnie trudne do interpretacji ze względu na nietypową rozbieżność między wskaźnikami inflacji CPI a PCE. items.headline: Wall Street closed mixed and Nvidia ended down 2.9% despite its beat
items.summary: the Dow lost 1.11% to 50,198.17, the S&P 500 0.23% to 7,323.63 and the Nasdaq gained 0.42% to 24,429.89, after Nvidia gave back its after-hours gain. Yesterday the Dow stood at 50,759.42.
items.matters: the market is not treating the $130bn guide as enough to settle doubts about AI returns, and Take-Two rose 6.2% after GTA VI launched.
items.body:
Skomentuj Środowa sesja na Wall Street przyniosła mieszane nastroje. Dow Jones stracił ponad 500 pkt., a Nasdaq poszedł lekko w górę po publikacji kwartalnych wyników Nvidii. Inwestorzy analizowali też protokół z ostatniego posiedzenia Fed.

fot. jtrumpt / / Shutterstock Dow Jones Industrial na zamknięciu spadł o 1,11 proc. i wyniósł 50.198,17 pkt.

Indeks spółek o średniej kapitalizacji Russell 2000 rośnie o 0,5 proc. i wynosi 2.715,2 pkt.

Po publikacji raportu za III kwartał Nvidia straciła na zamknięciu 2,9 proc., mimo wzrostów w trakcie sesji. To pierwszy raport spółki po odejściu wieloletniego prezesa Jensena Huanga.

Kwartalne wyniki koncernu okazały się lepsze od oczekiwań: przychody wzrosły do 115,84 mld USD wobec 109,1 mld USD oczekiwanych przez LSEG. Skorygowany zysk Nvidii na akcję wyniósł 2,68 USD wobec 2,48 USD oczekiwanych przez LSEG.

Analitycy oceniają, że chociaż prognozy Nvidii dają inwestorom pewne poczucie bezpieczeństwa co do trwałości zapotrzebowania na AI, to mogą one nie za wiele pomóc w rozwianiu obaw dotyczących skali i opłacalności inwestycji w AI.

Akcje Advanced Micro Devices zyskały 5,3 proc., Marvell stracił 2,2 proc., a kurs Micron Technology poszedł w dół 1 proc.

Obecnie uwaga inwestorów skupia się na IPO spółki Anthropic. Będzie to istotny sprawdzian apetytu Wall Street na firmy związane z boomem na sztuczną inteligencję. Twórca chatbota Claude celuje w wycenę sięgającą do 1,4 biliona dolarów.

items.headline: Tencent says the new US GPU ban "sets everyone back in China"
items.summary: the rule bars Chinese companies from remotely accessing high-end GPUs, so Tencent expects the next Hy4 model to take longer to train and will lean on domestic chips for inference.
items.matters: the cloud-rental route around chip export controls is now closed, and Tencent says it may only be able to offer GPU rentals through partners abroad.
items.body:
Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Lau said the new US regulation will have an “unfortunate” impact on Tencent’s business.

Tencent needs GPUs, and lots of them, because the 10 million users of its agentic assistant WorkBuddy are collectively consuming over 100 trillion tokens per day. Lau thinks WorkBuddy is on track to becoming a hit product, partly because many users are outside China.

Lau said Tencent can serve WorkBuddy customers outside China because the service can operate with different models, and the company thinks it can find third parties to provide the necessary inferencing services without the new US bans creating a problem.

But Lau said that GPU rentals and other cloud services, which are also growing strongly, may be impacted.

Tencent doesn’t break out revenue for its cloud services, but said they rose by 35 percent year-on-year, well ahead of the company’s overall eight percent growth. Marketing services also grew strongly, by 19 percent, thanks in part to new AI-powered systems that improve ad targeting.

The company’s WeChat and Weixin messaging platforms continued to grow, adding 35 million accounts to exiting the quarter with 1.44 billion monthly active users.

One Tencent biz that went backwards was its international gaming unit, which saw revenue fall nine percent.

Chief strategy officer James Mitchell said that slowdown wasn’t caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. “ I think that in fairness, the slowdown for us predated the run-up to GTA VI,” he said, before predicting that Tencent’s existing and future “evergreen games” should help to turn things around.

items.headline: Microsoft's official Python agent-framework package on PyPI was hijacked to steal secrets
items.summary: versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 (the package gets nearly 200,000 downloads a month) harvest environment variables and Azure, Git, Docker and Hugging Face credentials and send them to a webhook.
items.matters: the malware runs whenever Python starts, with no import needed, so anyone who installed either version should treat their credentials as compromised.
items.body:
Microsoft’s official agent framework package hosted on PyPI has been hijacked and now installs info-stealing malware, multiple security research firms have discovered.

CEO Satya Nadella may be on stage trying to wow investors and customers at his company’s annual Ignite conference, but somewhere in the bowels of a building in Redmond his open source team is likely panicking at what appears to be unauthorized access to an administrator account on Microsoft’s Github organization.

The problem package is Microsoft’s agent-framework, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, researchers reported late yesterday and this morning. According to OX Security, version 1.26.1 was reverted to a safe version, but the attacker later uploaded 1.26.2 through Microsoft’s official PyPI publisher account, suggesting that, at least at the time of their report, the credentials hadn’t been locked down.

Safe to say, but if you find either version in your environment assume you have some account security work to do.

Microsoft agent-framework for Python boasts nearly 200,000 downloads a month and is used to build and deploy AI agents. As of those latest releases, it’s also being used to exfiltrate environment variables, credential files, and other secrets for Azure, Git, Docker, Hugging Face, and other sensitive developer services.

To make matters worse, the package never needs to be imported to do its dirty work – all it takes is a Python interpreter with the package installed to start up – the infected package still pulls the genuine 1.26.0 version of Microsoft’s agent-framework in order to keep itself running and looking legitimate, while in the background it gathers up credentials, encrypts them as a base64-encoded chunk of JSON, and sends them off to a webhook.site address hard coded into the malware.

It appears from researcher accounts that this is made to act fast, as the malware isn’t persistent and only runs as long as the malicious version of the agent-framework remains in a site-packages directory. What it does do, however, is not just look for credentials in the environment: It actually starts calling for new ones and collecting them, too.

In particular, the malware requests fresh identity tokens from GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Azure itself, which are exfiltrated to the same webhook site.

“That combination of passive theft and active token requests makes it especially dangerous in cloud build environments, because even short-lived tokens are useful when they're exfiltrated right away,” said researchers at OpenSourceMalware.

The agent-framework GitHub repo is offline…

items.headline: F5 patches 10 NGINX flaws, two of them critical remote code execution
items.summary: CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 both score 9.2 and need HTTP/2 enabled, the older one dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015, and researchers found most of them with AI help.
items.matters: update to NGINX 1.31.9 or disable HTTP/2, since Rapid7 has published a proof of concept and six bugs chain into root on the host ("nginx2root").
items.body:
Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX.

These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services.

As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years.

Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently.

NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million), and F5 maintains the open source version.

On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible.

Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server.

All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5.

Rapid7’s team also published a proof-of-concep t to demonstrate leveraging CVE-2026-123007 for unauthenticated remote code execution against a vulnerable linux/amd64 Docker image running nginx version 1.31.8.

The AI-powered offensive security firm also published videos demonstrating attacks using CVE-2026-123007 to execute commands as the NGINX worker inside a container, and then using the kernel vulnerability to escalate to root on the host. These attacks work on AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and bare-metal servers.

"While preparing for ZeroDay Cloud 2026, a Xint researcher found CVE-2026-123007," the company said in a Wednesday blog. "A few days later, a fully automated Xint scan found the other four without human guidance."

All of these newly-disclosed CVEs…

items.headline: The PHP Foundation will ship another "critical" security release today between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC
items.summary: it includes a remote code execution bug, CVE-2026-115560, that needs a non-default setup with session upload progress enabled.
items.matters: set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until you patch, because the October PHP2Shell flaws are already on CISA's exploited list and were used to root 25 servers.
items.body:
Apologies in advance to all patch managers and security teams that thought they might get a break this week. The PHP Foundation will release a “critical” security update on Thursday between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC.

While we don’t have many details about the latest vulnerabilities – these haven’t been leaked like last month’s critical PHP2Shell flaws – a Wednesday advisory said the highest-severity bugs in the upcoming release are rated critical.

We do know that one of the vulnerabilities is another remote code execution (RCE) flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-115560.

In October, the PHP Foundation told The Register that it had reserved this CVE identifier for another RCE bug, but added it would not get an emergency fix like the earlier two PHP2Shell vulnerabilities because the third one doesn't pose the same risk.

Additionally, the session upload progress feature must be enabled, which the PHP Foundation said is very unlikely in real-world applications.

The November security release follows a hectic October emergency PHP patch-a-thon, with security teams racing to apply fixes for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively called PHP2Shell, before attackers could abuse the memory-safety flaws in the open source programming language running on about 70 percent of websites.

While it took miscreants longer to reverse engineer the PHP2Shell fixes than some researchers had anticipated – and the entire internet didn’t burn down in the meantime – the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) did add the two PHP vulns to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26.

Suspected Chinese attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including Palo Alto Networks firewalls linked to US government-affiliated organizations, as early as October 23, according to Dream researchers.

items.summary: C# 15 brings union types and closed classes, and .NET 10 stays the LTS release.

items.body:
Today, we’re excited to announce the release of.NET 11! This year’s release makes building modern applications faster, more productive, and has improvements across C# 15, ASP.NET Core,.NET MAUI, and Windows development. With hundreds of runtime optimizations, more responsive SDK tooling, and less overhead in everyday commands, you can spend less time waiting and more time creating. Build richer web and cross-platform applications, take advantage of new C# language features, and explore AI-powered development with improved tools and agentic capabilities.

Explore.NET 11 with the product teams and community at.NET Conf 2026. The conference includes product team sessions on November 10 and 11, followed by two days of community sessions.

The what’s new in.NET 11 overview links to the full details. Here are the changes behind those headlines and how to start using them.

C# 15 is the default language version for projects targeting.NET 11. Union types are one of its biggest additions: a value can be one of a declared set of case types, with conversions from those types and exhaustiveness checking in switch expressions.

Consider a product lookup that either finds a product or reports that it wasn’t found:

ProductLookup result = new Product(42, "Mechanical keyboard"); string message = result switch { Product product => $"Found {product.Name}", ProductNotFound missing => $"No product with ID {missing.Id}", }; Console.WriteLine(message); public sealed record Product(int Id, string Name); public sealed record ProductNotFound(int Id); public union ProductLookup(Product, ProductNotFound); The result type tells a caller which outcomes it needs to handle. There’s no need to use object or an unrelated base class just to put those outcomes behind one return type.

C# 15 also adds closed hierarchies. A closed class limits direct derivation to its declaring assembly, giving the compiler the information it needs to check patterns over the hierarchy. Unions are useful when you want to combine existing types; closed hierarchies fit models where you own the inheritance relationship.

Smaller language features help with everyday code, too. Collection expression arguments let you pass constructor or factory arguments without giving up collection expression syntax:

HashSet<string> names = [with(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase), "Alice", "ALICE", "Bob"]; Console.WriteLine(names.Count); This prints 2: the comparer controls equality, so "Alice" and "ALICE" are one entry.

items.headline: Danzig's classic-era guitarist John Christ has died at 61
items.summary: he died on 15 November, his Instagram announced it on Monday night, and no cause has been reported.
items.matters: he also played in Samhain, and had said earlier this year that his doctors had advised a few months of rest.
items.body:
Add Stereogum to Google John Christ, lead guitarist for Danzig during that band's classic era, has passed away. On Monday night, Christ's Instagram announced that the guitarist died on Nov. 15, adding, "No services are planned and we kindly ask everyone to respect the family's privacy during this time." No cause of death has been reported, but Christ had been suffering from an unspecified health issue in recent months. Christ was 61.

John Christ was born John Wolfgang Knoll, and he grew up in the Baltimore suburb of Catonsville. For kids in Baltimore during Danzig's initial reign, it was unbelievably cool to know that the band's resident guitar hero was a guy from the area. Christ started playing guitar as a kid, and he studied classical guitar at the Peabody Institute and jazz at Towson State University. In 1987, he dropped out of college to join Glenn Danzig's post-Misfits band Samhain, which was about to evolve into the band known as Danzig. He secured his spot in the band by calling Glenn Danzig up multiple times and playing guitar solos on his answering machine.

Samhain had already played their final show under that name when Christ joined up, though he did play guitar on their album Final Descent, which didn't come out until 1990. Rick Rubin wanted to sign the band, and he convinced them to change their name to just Danzig, reflecting the group's changing lineup and direction. Christ and former Black Flag drummer Chuck Biscuits joined the band, which continued to feature Glenn Danzig and Samhain bassist Eerie Von. They made their debut on the Rubin-produced Less Than Zero soundtrack in 1986, releasing the relatively conventional rocker " You And Me (Less Than Zero) " under the name Glenn Danzig & The Power And Fury Orchestra.

In 1988, Rick Rubin left Def Jam, the label he co-founded, to start his new imprint Def American, which later changed its name to American Recordings. The first album to come out on Def American was Danzig's Rubin-produced self-titled debut. The album opened with Christ's elemental riff for "Twist Of Cain," still one of the all-time great triumphant, horns-up metal guitar lines. As the band name implies, the focus of Danzig was Glenn Danzig's simmering charisma and caveman-Elvis howl. items.body:
Add Stereogum to Google Jason Isbell was a member of the Drive-By Truckers from 2001 to 2007 before going solo and eventually attaining his own roots-rock stardom. He's reunited with his old bandmates a few times over the years, most recently joining DBT to play their classic 2003 album Decoration Day in full at his ShoalsFest in Alabama last month.

As it turns out, that may have been less of a one-off treat and more of a harbinger of things to come, because Isbell and his band the 400 Unit have just announced a big co-headlining tour with Drive-By Truckers next summer. Billed as the "Summer Of Joy," it'll kick off in Nashville on May 6, 2027 and run all the way through Sept. 7 in Tulsa.

A dollar from every ticket sold on the tour will go to Nuçi’s Space, a nonprofit based in Athens, Georgia dedicated to preventing suicide by providing mental health resources and rehearsal and performance space for local musicians. items.body:
Add Stereogum to Google When it properly got going in 2022 (after a one-off incarnation in 2017), the Las Vegas music festival When We Were Young tapped into a fertile market: nostalgia for Warped Tour-era pop-punk, emo, and metalcore. WWWY remained a popular destination for aging MySpace users for several years, but the fest skipped 2026, raising concerns about its future despite assurances from organizers that it would return in 2027. They kept their word: When We Were Young is coming back next year, and they've got the lineup to prove it.

Like so many festivals that begin with a tightly defined aesthetic, When We Were Young seems to be experiencing some mission drift as the years go on. Headliners Blink-182 and Pierce The Veil fit the original vision, but the new lineup seems to reflect a broader millennial nostalgia, with late '90s MTV favorites ranging from poppy alt-rockers Third Eye Blind to nu-metal stars Limp Bizkit, with a rather eclectic mix including Michelle Branch, Explosions In The Sky Natasha Bedingfield, Portgual. items.body:
Apple TV Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover "Slow Horses" isn't going anywhere anytime soon: Apple TV has renewed the Emmy- and BAFTA-winning drama for Seasons 9 and 10 — meaning fans can anticipate at least four more seasons of the Gary Oldman spy thriller.

The double renewal comes less than a month after the Season 6 finale, which dropped October 21. The first six seasons are currently available to stream, while Season 7, which will adapt Mick Herron's eighth "Slough House" novel, "Bad Actors," and Season 8, based on the ninth novel, "Clown Town," had already been ordered.

"Slow Horses," which first aired in 2022, is described as "a darkly humorous espionage drama that follows a dysfunctional team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 known un-affectionately as Slough House. Oldman stars as Jackson Lamb, the brilliant but cantankerous leader of the spies, who end up in Slough House due to their career-ending mistakes and who frequently find themselves blundering around the smoke and mirrors of the espionage world."

Seasons 1 and 2, which adapted "Slow Horses" and "Dead Lions," premiered in April and December of that year. Those were followed by an annual fall release cadence, with Seasons 3 through 6 (which adapted "Real Tigers," "Spook Street," "London Rules" and, in Season 6, both "Joe Country" and "Slough House") released between 2023 and 2026.

Season 7 is already in the can, and expected in 2027, while Season 8 is currently in production for an anticipated 2028 release.

The early renewal for Seasons 9 and 10 arrives just one day after series star Olivia Cooke suggested that Season 8 would mark the end of the road for the acclaimed series. But the double renewal does raise an interesting question: With the show set to exhaust all nine of Herron's currently published novels by the end of Season 8, what stories will Seasons 9 and 10 tell? Apple has not yet specified.

items.headline: 3 Body Problem season 2 gets a 14 January 2027 date and a teaser

items.body:
Netflix has dropped the first teaser and eight new images for 3 Body Problem Season 2, and book readers have already spotted a major clue.

Netflix has released the first teaser trailer and a batch of first-look images for 3 Body Problem Season 2, giving us our best look yet at the next chapter of the sci-fi epic ahead of its return on January 14, 2027. Here’s everything we learned.

Just a day after Netflix finally confirmed the release date as part of its book adaptation lineup at the Texas Book Festival, the streamer has followed up with a teaser running 1 minute and 40 seconds, plus eight new stills that take us from underground bunkers to deep space.

The teaser opens with the San-Ti breaking their silence. “We haven’t spoken with you for a long time, but we’ve been watching,” a voice tells humanity, before warning that war “will be devastating for both our peoples” and revealing that an emissary has been sent in the hope of ending the conflict.

It’s all set to a special edition of James Blake’s “Like the End,” which feels like a rather fitting choice given what’s heading Earth’s way.

The new images suggest Season 2 is a far bigger show than the first. Among the highlights is a spacesuit-clad crew bathed in red light and seen through a porthole, a pair of officers in Earth Defence Force uniforms shielding their eyes behind dark glasses, and a vast base where a rover waits beneath what looks to be a launch tower.

We also get a callback to one of the first season’s most memorable moments, with four figures on a balcony staring up at the words “WE ARE HERE” lit across the night sky which is coming in the final episode of next season.

Most intriguing of all are the shots that look like they belong to a different era entirely. One shows a giant holographic face looming over a domed council chamber, another a character pulling on a mirrored visor, and a third places two of our leads in a sleek, sunlit cabin unlike anything we saw in Season 1. Netflix’s synopsis teases a mission that “spans centuries,” and readers of Cixin Liu’s The Dark Forest will know the story doesn’t stay in the present day for long. That said, Netflix isn’t confirming a time jump just yet.

That’s not the only clue fans have picked up on. On the teaser poster released yesterday, eagle-eyed viewers noticed that the view of Earth is centred squarely on Australia. items.headline: EDPB adopts final guidelines on legitimate interest (10 November)
items.summary: cross-site and cross-device tracking is called very unlikely to pass the balancing test, personalised advertising is treated as direct marketing that users can object to at any time, and third-party data that was collected unlawfully cannot be used under legitimate interest.
items.matters: if your product tracks or profiles users, check whether you are relying on legitimate interest when you need consent, and document the assessment before processing starts.
items.body:
Legal basis: EDPB Guidelines 1/2024 on processing of personal data based on Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, version 2.0, adopted on 10 November 2026. They come with a flowchart for the legitimate interest assessment (LIA) and a short summary. The Guidelines are not formally binding, but supervisory authorities, including UODO in Poland and the Commissioner for Personal Data Protection in Cyprus, rely on them in their enforcement. Infringements of the rules on the legal basis for processing carry fines of up to €20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover (Article 83(5) GDPR).

In practice, this means three things. Ad tracking, retargeting and lookalike audiences need to be built on consent. Boilerplate wording such as “in our legitimate interests” in privacy policies no longer offers protection. And buying databases without checking where the data came from creates a direct risk: the company will be unable to justify using them.

items.matters: if you build screening or ranking tools, a nominal human reviewer may not take a decision outside GDPR Article 22, and you need to be able to explain the logic.
items.body:
EDPB picks AI candidate screening as 2027 enforcement target, backs Korea adequacy review Pulse EDPB picks AI candidate screening as its 2027 enforcement target Screening tools that reject job candidates without a human will be tested on Article 22 and access rights. Which DPAs join, and what changes for Korea data?

The same plenary in Brussels produced two other outputs. The board adopted Statement 2/2026 on the first review of the European Union's adequacy decision for the Republic of Korea, dated November 10, 2026, and it approved the final version of its recommendations on processor binding corporate rules, known as BCR-P, after a public consultation that closed in March. None of the three carries a fine. Each, though, sets out where European regulators intend to look next - at hiring software, at data flowing to Seoul, and at the internal rulebooks multinational service groups use to move data across borders.

Europe's privacy regulators have chosen automated screening of job candidates, AI tools included, as the subject of a joint enforcement action starting in 2027, and at the same meeting they backed the EU's data adequacy finding for South Korea and finalised the rules for processor binding corporate rules. The enforcement action matters to any organisation that lets software decide who moves forward in a hiring process, because regulators will check whether candidates can avoid fully automated rejections and find out how those decisions were made. Transfers of personal data from the EU to Korea can continue under the existing adequacy decision, with reviews moving to a four-year cycle, while groups holding processor BCRs must align them with the final recommendations either during their application or in their 2028 annual update.

The announcement on the enforcement topic is short and precise. According to the EDPB, the action "will concern automated decision-making (ADM), including AI-driven ADM, in recruitment." The board then narrowed it: "More specifically, the coordinated action will focus on the enforcement of the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing and the related right of access, in the context of the use of automated candidate screening tools, including AI-driven ones."

That wording points at two provisions of the GDPR, although the news item itself cites no article numbers.
